_comment: From agent-brain/templates. Hooks point at core/helpers (submodule). Marketplace/plugins: enter once, installation happens on the next start. The marketplace below is an EXAMPLE — replace 'your-org' with the marketplace repo that pins this core for your setup.

permissions._comment: A new brain's default scope is the core ONLY — additional suites are enabled/installed exclusively on explicit operator request. The allowlist covers self-setup and self-analysis (core scripts/helpers, git reads, committing, plugin checks) and the everyday collaboration path: push (also `git -C <repo>`, the form working rule #8 prescribes for a neighbour repo), pull requests and issues. A push used to stay ask: measured 2026-10-16 on a collaborator's brain, every commit and push raised a dialog the human did not understand, and the AI read push as 'needs the operator' — the merge and publish gates (mechanism-guard, operator-only list) carry the real limits, not a permission dialog. Kept asking: settings edits, and a push that names `main` (a bare `git push` matches nothing here and is allowed — an instance whose ordered main push is a named form puts that form under its own allow). `gh pr merge` has no rule on purpose: the classifier and mechanism-guard decide merges. Denied: force pushes (`--force`, `-f`, `+ref`) and branch deletes with `--delete`. A delete spelled `:ref` has NO rule here: a pattern ending in `:*` is read as the legacy prefix form (`Bash(git push * :*)` would be a prefix match, not a glob), so it cannot be written safely; that spelling stays a known gap. `gh issue *` includes `gh issue delete` — a decision, not an oversight. The git/gh rules exist twice, as `Bash(...)` and as `PowerShell(...)`: on Windows Claude Code offers both tools, a Bash rule does not reach the PowerShell tool, and a Bash DENY rule switches the PowerShell tool off for the whole session unless a scoped PowerShell rule exists (docs: tools-reference, 'PowerShell tool'; permissions, 'PowerShell' — read 2026-10-16). PowerShell rules have the same shape as Bash rules (`*` anywhere, `:*` as trailing ` *`), so the strings are identical. The core-script rules stay Bash-only: the core's scripts are run from Git Bash (working rule #8, OS-trap register). The core update path is allowed too, so the AI updates and switches the core channel by itself: `claude plugin update`, `claude plugin marketplace update`, and `claude plugin enable|disable|install brain-core*` — the channel switch goes through the CLI, never through a hand edit of `enabledPlugins` (that stays ask with every other settings edit); other suites are still enabled and installed only on the operator's word, hence the `brain-core` prefix. `claude plugin update *` reaches every installed plugin, not only the core — deliberate: an update follows the marketplace pin and adds nothing that was not installed before; the prefix `brain-core*` also matches other names starting that way, which is accepted because a foreign plugin still needs its marketplace added, and that stays ask. Like the core-script rules, the update path is Bash-only: it runs from Git Bash on Windows, so these entries have no PowerShell twins. Also allowed: `git -C core remote set-url --push origin DISABLED`, the push block for a core checkout that still carries old history. Measured 2026-10-18 on a macOS brain moving to 2.0.0: in auto mode the classifier refused the channel switch ('Self-Modification') and the push block ('Remote Repoint') even after the operator's word in chat, so every core update needed the human at the keyboard. `.claude/rules/feedback.md` is under ask although `.claude/rules/**` is allowed: it holds the operator's binding corrections, and an AI that writes them edits its own rules. Measured 2026-10-22 on a macOS brain in auto mode: the classifier refused writing an operator correction there three times ('Self-Modification', 'Instruction Poisoning' twice) — an allow rule did not help, the correction was lost between chat and file. With the rule under ask the operator sees each entry in a dialog and confirms it (operator decision 2026-10-22: 'always interactive, with confirmation'). The protocol that records the operator's words stays free: it is a log, not a rule.
allow: Bash(git -C core remote set-url --push origin DISABLED)
